title: Add conversational RAG CLI with tool-scratchpad and reproducible eval harness
author: Priya Narang
description: Introduce a lightweight conversational RAG CLI that demonstrates tool-calling with a writable 'scratchpad' for intermediate tool outputs, plus a small reproducible eval harness and updated docs. Motivation: provide an end-to-end developer example for debugging multi-tool agent behavior in a terminal environment and for writing scenario-based regressions that run in CI. What this PR adds: - examples/rag/cli-scratchpad/: TypeScript Node CLI with an interactive REPL, command palette for tools (search/index/query tool, http-fetch, file-preview), and a persisted scratchpad for each session. - examples/rag/cli-scratchpad/README.md: quickstart and config (Redwood API key, model pinning, streaming). - docs/quickstarts/conversational-cli.md: step-by-step guide, recommended prompts, and telemetry knobs. - tests/e2e/rag-cli-replay/: replayable scenarios (JSONL) plus a harness that runs the CLI in headless mode and asserts tool invocations and final output. - examples/telemetry/probes/cli-session-telemetry.yaml: sample probe definitions for Console/ConsoleAgent metrics. - package.json updates for the examples workspace, with a small test script and 'replay' target. Checklist: - [x] CLI implementation with tool interface and scratchpad persistence - [x] E2E replay harness and three baseline scenarios - [x] Docs quickstart and inline examples - [x] CI job added to run replay scenarios under node 18 and 20 - [x] minimal linting and type fixes requested in review Usage example: node ./examples/rag/cli-scratchpad/bin/run --api-key=$REDWOOD_KEY --model=gpt-small --session=demo-session Key design notes: - Scratchpad is a per-session append-only log that tools can write to; the agent can read the scratchpad as part of the context window for subsequent calls. This is intentionally simple to show tradeoffs (consistency vs. throughput). - Reproducible evals are JSONL scenarios that include user inputs, simulated tool responses (when offline), and expected assertions. The harness can run in CI without network by consuming canned tool responses. - Docs include guidance on turning this into a canary regression (baseline recordings + delta assertion). Related work: builds on the labbed RAG examples and the replay harness pattern used by the rag-session-replayer; references ENG-2145 for agent tooling ergonomics. Notes on CI: initial run failed on node 20 due to a flaky timing assumption in the headless runner; added a backoff/retry and pinned test to use process signals; CI now passes on rerun. Merge method: squash. Release notes: "Add conversational RAG CLI example with tool-scratchpad, replayable eval scenarios, and docs quickstart; useful for developer debugging and CI regression testing."
